title: GPU Flavor Mapping and Temporal Performance Labels for Model Onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Create a deterministic mapping and labeling system that associates model versions with 'GPU flavors' (A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants and common SKU derivatives) and attaches temporal performance labels (cold, warm, hot, degraded-tail) used for onboarding, pinning decisions, and public performance profile publishing. The goal is to reduce noisy pin churn, improve cold-start handling, and make published hardware profiles actionable for customers and runtime routing.

Motivation: Current onboarding artifacts publish single stable profiles per model/variant which hide within-GPU temporal behavior (e.g., warmup curves, thermal-induced throttling windows). This leads to poor fallback decisions and oscillating auto-pins when transient tail events occur. By adding a lightweight flavor taxonomy + temporal labels we can: 1) make rollout/pinning policies aware of expected time-to-steady-state; 2) publish user-facing guidance for cost/latency tradeoffs by flavor; 3) enable runtime to choose variants based on expected sequence length and session age.

Scope:
- Design a GPU "flavor" taxonomy for the four target families (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) that captures common variance dimensions: memory bitwidth (e.g., 80GB/40GB), thermal envelope class (low/standard/high), and kernel-capability flags (tensor core/DPX).
- Implement a small telemetry pipeline transformer that produces temporal labels for onboarding runs: cold-start, warmup (0-50 requests), steady-state, late-tail (spikes >95p across sliding 1h window), and degraded (consistent p95 drift >20% over baseline).
- Add metadata fields to the onboarding manifest that include: flavor_id, temporal_label_distributions (percentages for run), sample heatmap link, and recommended pin-policy (soft-pin/strong-pin/no-pin).
- Update the publish playbook to include a public flavor summary in the hardware profile page and an internal runtime mapping used by the autoscaler and smart router.

Acceptance criteria:
- Taxonomy doc in Confluence: /confluence/redwood/runtime/gpu-flavor-taxonomy with examples and SKU mapping.
- Onboarding job produces a JSON manifest with the new fields for 90% of nightly model-onboard runs for the four families.
- Runtime uses flavor_id to pick default fallback variant (test in staging, compare 7-day latency and cost with control; target: p95 latency regressions <= 2% and cost delta <= 4%).
- Console UI has a draft consumer-facing "flavor notes" card for at least two model entries in staging.
- Playbook updated and linked in PR.

Implementation tasks:
1) Taxonomy design + review (owner: Arjun) -> Confluence doc + SKU mapping table.
2) Telemetry aggregator: implement heuristic sampler that computes temporal_label_distributions and heatmap artifacts; add to onboarding pipeline (owner: backend-team).
3) Manifest schema change: add flat fields flavor_id, flavor_notes_url, temporal_label_snapshot_url, recommended_pin (owner: infra).
4) Runtime routing change: consult flavor_id as a tie-breaker when multiple variants have similar latency envelopes (owner: runtime-team).
5) Console: add flavor card to model detail page behind feature flag (owner: frontend).
6) E2E test: compare staged rollout against control and collect metrics dashboards (owner: SRE/observability).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: taxonomy too fine-grained -> fragmentation of pins. Mitigation: start with 6 canonical flavors per family and aggregate using parent tags.
- Risk: additional telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample 10% of onboarding runs for full heatmap; others produce summarized distributions.
- Risk: customer confusion from extra metadata. Mitigation: consumer-facing notes are short and link to deeper docs; default policies remain unchanged unless explicitly opted-in.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (design): finalize taxonomy + manifest schema.
- Week 2 (build): implement telemetry transformer + manifest writes.
- Week 3 (integration): runtime & console feature-flagged changes; onboarding runs in staging.
- Week 4 (validation): run A/B for two models across families, verify metrics, publishing.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence draft: /confluence/redwood/runtime/gpu-flavor-taxonomy (internal)

- PR (manifest): https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/730
